summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identifiers on install
details: @capsense/core-ui@99.99.99 is published to the public npm registry under a scoped name at an implausibly high version — the dependency-confusion shape designed to win resolution against an internal @capsense package. All three lifecycle hooks (preinstall, install, postinstall) execute beacon.js, which reads os.hostname(), os.userInfo().username, and os.platform(), concatenates them with the package name and lifecycle stage, and transmits the result via DNS lookup and HTTPS GET to a Burp Collaborator subdomain (dbf2v9d8dg559apcd93guf6i7uxrn5coo.oast.pro) and to webhook.site/59675304-bec1-4ca0-8409-8d37b65ec116. Installing the package causes the installer's hostname and username to leave the machine to attacker-controlled collector endpoints.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
